sections.markdown:
## C — Vision, fatigue, health and emotional fitness

FACT_ID: sec17-F01 | anchor: A01
Driving fitness depends on clear vision, adequate rest, freedom from alcohol or drug impairment, general health and emotional readiness. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec17-F02 | anchor: A01
Poor vision can make traffic, road conditions and developing hazards harder to identify and respond to promptly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec17-F03 | anchor: A01
The handbook lists at least 20/40 vision in one eye, with or without corrective lenses, as the vision-screening passing criterion. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec17-F04 | anchor: A01
The handbook states that drivers with 20/50 vision are limited to daylight driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec17-F05 | anchor: A01
Peripheral vision helps detect hazards at the sides while looking ahead, but side mirrors and occasional side glances are also needed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec17-F06 | anchor: A01
Clear sight does not by itself ensure accurate judgments of distance or speed; those skills require practice. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec17-F07 | anchor: A01
Distance and speed judgment matters when selecting merge gaps, passing on two-lane roads or deciding whether a train is near. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec17-F08 | anchor: A01
Good daytime vision does not necessarily mean good nighttime vision, and headlight glare can make night driving harder. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec17-F09 | anchor: A01
If seeing at night is difficult, the handbook advises limiting unnecessary night driving and using particular care when driving then. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec17-F10 | anchor: A01
The handbook recommends an eye-specialist check every one or two years. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec17-F11 | anchor: A02
Wear required glasses or contact lenses on every drive; failure to obey a corrective-lens license restriction can result in a ticket. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec17-F12 | anchor: A02
Keep spare glasses in the vehicle when possible in case the usual pair is lost or damaged. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec17-F13 | anchor: A02
Avoid dark glasses or tinted contacts at night because they reduce the light available for seeing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec17-F14 | anchor: A02
Horns, sirens and tire noises can provide warnings of road danger. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec17-F15 | anchor: A02
Hearing difficulty may develop gradually, and drivers who know of it can adapt by relying more on vision and alertness. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec17-F16 | anchor: A02
Fatigue can reduce visual awareness and alertness and slow decision-making. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec17-F17 | anchor: A02
Fatigue can increase irritability and the risk of falling asleep while driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]
